title: Video Editor
description:
Role Title: Video Editor (AI Video Annotation)
Role Type: Contractor, Remote
Location: North America, Latin America, Europe, UK, and Oceania
micro1 is engaging Video Editors for a project focused on reviewing and annotating video sessions of robotic arms completing real-world tasks. This is an AI training and video annotation project rather than a traditional editing or post-production assignment.
Your ability to analyze footage frame by frame, recognize timing and continuity, and notice small visual changes translates directly to this work. You will identify and label actions, events, and outcomes with precision, helping create reliable training data for next-generation AI systems. No prior experience in AI, robotics, or data annotation is required-your visual judgment and editing background are what matter.
Scope of Work

• Review video footage of robotic arms performing tasks, following detailed annotation and grading guidelines provided by the customer.

• Identify and label actions, object interactions, transitions, task outcomes, errors, and other relevant events within each video segment.

• Apply frame-by-frame analysis, timing awareness, and continuity judgment to determine when actions begin, change, and end.

• Use dedicated annotation tools to mark video events precisely and consistently.

• Flag unclear footage, visual inconsistencies, or ambiguous moments and document your observations in concise written notes.

• Contribute to quality control by reviewing annotations and providing constructive feedback when requested.

• Complete assigned batches accurately and within established deadlines.

Preferred Qualifications

• Professional or academic background in video editing, post-production, filmmaking, audiovisual production, or a related field.

• Experience reviewing footage closely for timing, continuity, movement, and visual consistency.

• Familiarity with editing software such as Adobe Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, Final Cut Pro, Avid Media Composer, or similar tools.

• Excellent attention to detail and the ability to maintain accuracy during repetitive frame-level review.

• Strong written communication skills, with the ability to document visual observations clearly and objectively.

• Experience with video annotation, visual QA, AI training projects, or robotics is helpful but not required.

title: Program Manager I, El Niño Preparedness EMPOWER/RAPID
description:
Job Summary
The Program Manager I will provide program management, technical, and coordination support to EMPOWER partners in South America to strengthen El Niño preparedness and readiness for rapid, partner-led emergency response. The position will support implementation of preparedness activities across priority countries and hotspots, helping translate hazard, vulnerability, market, operational, and partner-capacity information into practical readiness actions, quality program designs, and activation-ready response plans.
Working under the guidance of the Program Manager II and in coordination with technical, MEAL, supply chain, finance, safeguarding, and operations colleagues, the Program Manager I will accompany partners to complete priority preparedness deliverables, address program bottlenecks, test readiness arrangements, and maintain country-level materials that can be rapidly adapted when an EMPOWER/RAPID response is activated.
Roles and Key Responsibilities

• Support implementation of the El Niño preparedness workplans across assigned South America countries or hotspots in coordination with EMPOWER partners, country teams, RAPID counterparts, and technical and operational colleagues.

• Maintain detailed activity plans, deliverable trackers, meeting records, and follow-up actions that connect program, MEAL, partnership, cash and voucher assistance, supply chain, finance, safeguarding, and operational readiness tasks.

• Compile and synthesize available hazard, vulnerability, exposure, seasonal, and scenario information to help identify priority locations, population groups, likely needs, access constraints, and preparedness triggers for drought, floods, food insecurity, wildfires, and related El Niño impacts.

• Support stakeholder and service mapping with partners, including government authorities, Caritas structures, humanitarian coordination bodies, community actors, technical services, financial service providers, and other response stakeholders.

• Facilitate partner working sessions to develop or update country- and hotspot-specific contingency plans, response strategies, sector and modality options, targeting approaches, geographic priorities, and scalable response scenarios.

• Gather technical inputs and support documentation of minimum program quality standards, intervention packages, eligibility and prioritization criteria, referral pathways, assistance quantities or transfer values, and safe adaptation or substitution rules.

• Coordinate routine follow-up with supply chain and operations colleagues so proposed relief kits, in-kind assistance, and cash or voucher options reflect assessed needs, market capacity, cultural appropriateness, protection considerations, delivery feasibility, lead times, and cost drivers.

• Incorporate validated market and logistics findings into program drafts, implementation schedules, modality recommendations, delivery sequencing, contingency options, and procurement inputs.

• Support partner readiness for cash and voucher assistance, including participant-data requirements, accountability and complaints mechanisms, protection and inclusion measures, reconciliation processes, monitoring, and failed-payment follow-up.

• Prepare and update activation-ready program materials, including rapid assessment tools, response concept drafts, targeting and registration approaches, implementation plans, staffing assumptions, budget inputs, procurement requests, risk registers, and donor narrative inputs.

• Monitor assigned preparedness activities and any activated response tasks, flag delays or quality concerns, and support timely corrective action in line with CRS program quality principles and standards, donor requirements, and humanitarian good practice.

title: Generation Lead, Fuel-Based Generation
description:
ABOUT FLUIDSTACK

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.

We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

HOW WE OPERATE

- Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

- Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

- Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

- Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

- Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Power Generation Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

- Build an islanded grid at gigawatt scale, from a blank sheet. Generation, storage and compute running with no utility behind them, where the machine you design is the only thing holding voltage. No playbook exists at this size, so the architecture you set becomes the reference.

- Get power online in months, not years. Interconnection queues are measured in years and we do not have them. Generating our own power is how a site goes from signed lease to live compute inside six months, and the power system is the long pole in that plan.

- Make one power block, then build it a thousand times. A repeatable block and cluster unit, validated once and stamped across the fleet, is the only route to the scale we are targeting. Every bespoke site is schedule we do not get back.

- Design a grid whose largest load answers back. Compute is not passive demand here. Load behaviour, curtailment and shedding are design variables you negotiate and specify, a lever almost no power system engineer has ever been handed.

Role Scope

- Assess and qualify every fuel-oxidation generation technology worth considering for our blocks, from reciprocating engines and turbines to linear generators, and build the qualified technology and supplier list Fluidstack buys from.

- Set the standard interface that turns any engine, turbine or fuel cell into one interchangeable node in the site's decentralized generation array, with a defined electrical connection, control signals, telemetry and operating envelope, so the plant controller dispatches it alongside PV and BESS without bespoke integration.

- Decide how much fuel-based capacity each block carries, in what unit sizes and with what redundancy, for its firming and backup role, and hold that decision against cost, fuel use and uptime as the block design evolves.

- Write the technical specification and acceptance tests for each qualified unit, covering step-load acceptance, ramp rate, minimum load, start reliability, heat rate across the load range and emissions, and witness factory and site acceptance before a unit is accepted.

- Own installation and commissioning of the generation fleet through first fire, load testing against real AI load profiles and handover, and fold every field finding back into the specification.

title: IT System Administrator (m/f/d)
description:
ÜBER BUENA

Buena (finanziert von Google Ventures) macht alles rund um Immobilien so einfach und transparent wie den Kauf eines ETFs. Wir übernehmen deutschlandweit Hausverwaltungen und machen sie digital. In den vergangenen drei Jahren sind wir mit rund 25 Vollzeitmitarbeitern in Berlin zur zweitgrößten Hausverwaltung Deutschlands geworden.

 

ÜBER DIE ROLLE

Wir suchen einen Systemadministrator (m/f/d), der unsere IT im Griff hat. Dazu gehören das Google-Konto jedes Mitarbeitenden, jeder Laptop und das Netzwerk im Büro.

Mit jeder übernommenen Hausverwaltung wächst unsere IT. Deshalb braucht es jemanden, der Ordnung schafft und sie hält.

Du arbeitest direkt mit unserem Head of Product zusammen und bist erster Ansprechpartner für alle IT-Fragen im Büro.

VERANTWORTLICHKEITEN

Du sorgst dafür, dass unsere IT in Berlin rund läuft. Mittelfristig begleitest du auch die IT-Einbindung neu übernommener Hausverwaltungen. Das machst du gemeinsam mit unserem externen IT-Partner, damit jeder Standort unserem Standard entspricht.

 

GOOGLE WORKSPACE

- Du verwaltest Nutzer, Gruppen, Organisationseinheiten und Berechtigungen.

- Du pflegst die Sicherheitseinstellungen, zum Beispiel Zwei-Faktor-Anmeldung, Passwortregeln und Zugriffsrechte.

- Du verwaltest geteilte Ablagen, Freigaben und Lizenzen.

EIN- UND AUSTRITTE VON MITARBEITENDEN

- Du richtest neue Mitarbeitende ein: Konten, Lizenzen, Berechtigungen und Geräte.

- Du bereitest Laptops und Diensthandys vor und gibst sie aus.

- Wenn jemand das Unternehmen verlässt, entziehst du Zugänge, sicherst Daten und nimmst Geräte zurück.

- Du entwickelst diese Abläufe weiter und dokumentierst sie sauber.

GERÄTEVERWALTUNG

- Du verwaltest alle Geräte in NinjaOne. Dazu gehören Überwachung, Updates und Softwareverteilung.

- Apple-Geräte verwaltest du zusätzlich über den Apple Business Manager.

NETZWERK UND BÜRO-IT

- Du betreust unser Netzwerk am Hauptstandort, das auf Ubiquiti UniFi läuft.

- Du hilfst Kolleginnen und Kollegen vor Ort, von der einfachen Frage bis zur Fehlersuche.

DU PASST, WENN DU

- vor Ort in unserem Büro in Berlin (Prenzlauer Berg) arbeiten willst.

- sehr gut Deutsch und gut Englisch sprichst.

- eine Ausbildung als Fachinformatiker für Systemintegration oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation hast. Einschlägige Praxiserfahrung zählt genauso.

- mehrere Jahre Erfahrung in der Verwaltung von Google Workspace mitbringst.

- NinjaOne oder vergleichbare Software wie Jamf oder Intune kennst.

- dich mit macOS, iOS und dem Apple Business Manager auskennst.

- Grundkenntnisse in Netzwerktechnik hast, idealerweise mit UniFi.

DEINE BENEFITS

- Aufstiegschancen in einem der am schnellsten wachsenden Startups Europas.

- MacBook & Studio Display.

- Attraktives Gehalt, inklusive 500 € „Close-to-Office"-Bonus.

- 110 € Essenszuschuss und 50 € Fitnesszuschuss.

- Bücher: Buena zahlt jedes Buch, das du lesen willst.

- Tägliches Frühstück und Spezialitätenkaffee im Büro.

WARUM JETZT EINSTEIGEN

- Wir wachsen schnell mit einem kleinen Team: In den letzten 3 Jahren zur zweitgrößten Hausverwaltung Deutschlands mit rund 25 Vollzeitmitarbeitern.

- Wir sind meritokratisch: Wer liefert, bekommt Verantwortung. Unser CEO war vor 3 Jahren Junior Product Manager, unser COO vor 2 Jahren Chief of Staff.

- Wir bauen Buena langfristig auf: Die Wohneigentumsquote in Deutschland liegt weit unter dem europäischen Durchschnitt. Buena wird das ändern.

Work Deep Inside the Android Platform

• Ability to debug embedded systems where traditional step debugging may be limited or unavailable.

title: Senior/Lead DevOps / Observability Engineer
description:
About the client
Our client is a leading European online car marketplace, connecting car buyers and sellers across the continent. The platform serves over 30 million monthly users and operates across 18 countries, making it one of the largest and most trusted digital marketplaces for vehicles in Europe.
About the role
We are looking for a hands-on Observability / SRE Engineer with strong AWS infrastructure and networking skills to lead a focused, time-boxed migration of the monitoring setup for one application from New Relic to Grafana. You will be embedded in the client's engineering team, while owning the migration end to end and working independently as the sole engineer on this scope.
This is a short-term engagement with a clear deliverable. We value someone who can ramp up quickly, use modern AI-assisted tooling to move faster, communicate proactively with the team, and leave behind a clean, well-documented monitoring setup.
Responsibilities

• Assess the existing New Relic monitoring setup for the in-scope application, including dashboards, alerts, SLIs/SLOs, synthetic checks, and log and trace usage.

• Define the migration approach and map New Relic constructs to their Grafana-stack equivalents (Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, Tempo or similar).

• Rebuild dashboards and alert rules in Grafana, validating that coverage and alert quality match or improve on the current state.
Instrument and configure the application and its AWS infrastructure (such as compute, containers, load balancers, and managed services) to send metrics, logs, and traces to the new platform, using OpenTelemetry where applicable.

• Set up and validate secure network connectivity between AWS workloads and the Grafana stack, including VPC routing, security groups, VPC endpoints or PrivateLink, and DNS, and troubleshoot connectivity and data-flow issues.

• Run the old and new monitoring in parallel, verify data accuracy, and manage a safe cutover with minimal risk to production visibility; integrate and tune alerting with the team's incident and notification channels.

• Use AI-assisted development tools, including Codex, to improve engineering productivity and delivery speed, for example to translate queries, generate dashboards and configuration as code, and draft documentation, while reviewing and validating all output.

• Document the new setup, hand over knowledge to the team with runbooks, and keep stakeholders informed with regular progress updates and early risk flags.

Requirements

• 5+ years of experience in DevOps, SRE, or observability engineering, ideally in a high-traffic, cloud-based production environment.

• Strong hands-on experience with Grafana, including dashboard design, alerting, and data source configuration.

• Practical experience with New Relic (APM, dashboards, NRQL, alert policies) and a clear understanding of how to translate it to other tools.

• Experience with Prometheus (PromQL), log and trace tooling such as Loki, Tempo, or the ELK stack, and OpenTelemetry instrumentation.

• Solid hands-on experience with AWS infrastructure, such as EC2, EKS/ECS, IAM, CloudWatch, and S3, and with Infrastructure as Code (e.g., Terraform).

• Strong understanding of AWS networking, including VPC design, subnets, routing, security groups, load balancers, VPC endpoints/PrivateLink, and DNS (Route 53).

• Practical experience using AI-assisted development tools, such as Codex, in day-to-day engineering work.

• Proven ability to work independently and deliver within a tight timeline, with availability to work full-time within Canadian time zone hours and start on short notice.

• Excellent verbal and written English skills.

Nice to have

• Experience with Grafana Cloud or Grafana Mimir.

• Previous monitoring or observability tool migration projects.

• Experience defining SLIs/SLOs and error budgets.

• AWS certification (e.g., Solutions Architect, DevOps Engineer, or Advanced Networking)

NB! Working hours according to the Canadian Timez

🌟What the Job is All About
We are recruiting to fill Football Tracking System Technician roles within our expanding operations in the Serie A and Serie B. There may be opportunities to work across tournaments such as the UEFA Champions League and UEFA Europa League. This is an exciting opportunity to work at the forefront of sports technology as part of a dedicated and dynamic team.

Working day expectations:

- Match Day -> Arrival up to 6 hours pre-Kick Off

- Match Day -> End of day up to 1 hour post game completion

- There are also varied needs during the setup day/s which may require the assistants to be present on the day/s before match day.

- The role requires the consultant to be flexible with work hours depending on the needs of the onsite team

We are looking for committed and passionate people that are willing, and able to work throughout the football season. Please consider that this work is likely to be mostly on the weekend with some midweek fixtures.

We will equip you with the technical training, support and full exposure to our systems to perform your match day tasks but also encourage development and progression to help make an impact on what we do. Working as a Football Tracking Systems Technician, is a great entry level route into full time employment with Hawk-Eye Innovations ltd.
Please attach your CV in English

💼Key Responsibilities
The main purpose of this role is to prepare the tracking systems at the stadium and monitor them during the match. These systems are the Electronic Performance Tracking System (EPTS) and Goal-Line Technology (GLT).
You can find the more specific responsibilities here:

- Check that there is a fibre connection with all the switches in the stadium rooms and possibly resolve the problems by re-establishing the connections;

- Connect the EPTS room with the GLT/VAR (Video Assistant referee) van via the two networks .2 and .3;

- Set up and test communication via Dante with Replay Operator (RO), Assistant Replay Operator (ARO), Video Technical Guarantee (VTG) onsite and Technical Guarantee (TG) at the Remote Centre;

- Confirm with EPTS and GLT Remote Support that the system is working correctly and possibly follow the provisions deriving from this for troubleshooting;

- Calibrate the GLT system before the match, following the relevant checklist and carrying out all the necessary tests to test its reliability and precision;

title: Consulting AI Research Contributor
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Aptura is looking for Subject Matter Experts from management or strategy consulting, in an industry or functional practice, who build market sizing models, competitive landscapes and business cases in Excel. You have used AI tools on your own work and been frustrated by the mistakes they make. You will turn that experience into realistic Excel tasks that test how well AI does the work of a Consultant.

RESPONSIBILITIES

- Writing realistic Excel tasks drawn from your own work: extending existing models, fixing broken ones and building from a brief

- Working through each task yourself so there is a clear, correct answer

- Writing yes-or-no criteria precise enough that a grader can mark any attempt against them

NECESSARY QUALIFICATIONS

- 3+ years in management, strategy or operations consulting, in an industry practice (e.g. financial services, healthcare, TMT, consumer, energy, public sector) or a functional practice (strategy, operations, pricing, due diligence)

- Deep hands-on Excel: market sizing, competitive landscapes, goal seek, data reshaping and clear workbook structure

- Strong written English communication skills.

- Attention to detail, and willingness to learn concepts in AI and Evals

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

- Start Date : Immediate

- Duration: Approximately 4-6 weeks

- Payment: task-based. Experts who complete their first task within the required timeline will then be qualified to do multiple tasks for the remainder of the project.

CONTRACT AND PAYMENT TERMS

- You will be engaged as an independent contractor.

- This is a fully remote role that can be completed on your own schedule.

- Projects can be extended, shortened, or concluded early depending on needs and performance.

- Your work at Aptura will not involve access to confidential or proprietary information from any employer, client, or institution.

- Payments will be weekly following task completion.

GETTING STARTED

- Apply with your details and CV. Choose an available 30-minute group walkthrough call.

- Attend the walkthrough and create one original task from your own work. Submit the brief, the actual input workbook(s) needed to complete it. Input-file uploads are compulsory.

- Write the brief yourself. Input workbooks must also be human-built. Use real data that has been sanitised, or public data with the source named. No AI usage allowed.

- We run your task against current frontier AI models. If the models get it wrong, you then write a detailed yes-or-no rubric, and a reviewer signs off on the task with you.

- Completing onboarding does not guarantee a job offer; selection remains subject to written approval of the task proposal.

ABOUT APTURA

Aptura is an applied AI and data company working with frontier labs to train AI systems on real professional work. We do this by building high-quality evaluation and training environments that teach AI agents to produce work that can be used in daily workflows.

title: In-Home Physician Per Diem - Medford
description:
Job Title: In-Home Physician Per Diem - Medford
Job Location: Work at Home, Oregon, United States
Job Location Type: Remote
Job Contract Type: Part time
Job Seniority Level:
We’re building a world of health around every individual - shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger - helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.
Do you have a passion for engaging with people and helping them on their journey to better health? Signify Health, part of CVS Health®, is seeking a Per Diem Physician to provide In-Home Health Evaluations, engaging with people in the comfort of their own homes and helping bridge gaps in care.
You’ll play a critical role in building trusted relationships to make people healthier, helping bring flexible, comprehensive and personalized health evaluations right to people’s front doors.
Job highlights
The visit, which lasts about 45 minutes, allows for time to connect one-on-one and answer health questions. It includes a medication and medical history review, a physical evaluation, and, if ordered by the person’s health plan, additional diagnostic tests (i.e., diabetic eye exams, spirometry, etc.). You’ll use an iPad and an intuitive clinical workflow for each evaluation and are not required to prescribe medicine, order lab tests or alter people’s current treatment regimen.
In this role, you will:

• Bring your heart into every visit, joining a national network of purpose-driven clinicians dedicated to improving health outcomes

• Be part of our efforts to visit millions of people nationwide with the goal of providing connections to the right care for people’s unique needs

• Work with Signify Health as a clinician colleague, fulfilling the requirements of the specified role

• Be flexible to travel locally and within licensed states, as needed

• Conduct virtual visits as needed

• Provide all Signify Health services as indicated including Diagnostic & Preventive Services products (i.e., spirometry, DEE, bone density screening, etc.)

A Note on Our Work Environment:
As an in-home clinician, your primary workplace is the private residence of health plan members. We are dedicated to meeting health plan members where they are, wherever they call home. These environments are diverse and may present a variety of conditions. Candidates must be able to comfortably and safely perform their duties in homes that may contain household pets, secondhand smoke and other potential airborne allergens or irritants.
Why Clinicians Enjoy Working with Signify Health
“Many of the people I see are shocked that a physician is coming to their home to visit with them one-on-one. When you sit down and have an unhurried conversation about their health, they are impressed, happy, and understand that their health plan and care team cares about them.” - M.L., MD
“The primary care physician gets a snapshot of a person in an office setting, but with Signify Health, we see things like the number of steps to enter their home, the state of disrepair those steps may be in, and the person’s ability to function comfortably and with ease in their own home. We can make referrals to the individual’s health plan, encourage the participation of their loved ones, and ensure their PCPs are aware of their health and overall quality of life.” - C.H., MD
Per diem employees qualify for:

• Hourly base rate, plus additional incentive structure (i.e., per visit completed, other incentives may apply)

• Malpractice insurance coverage (during Signify Health-related activities)

• Supplies and other perks

Required & Preferred Qualifications (MDs and DOs)

• Active, unrestricted license(s) in coverage area(s)

• Multi-state licenses (preferred)

Anticipated Weekly Hours
12 Time

In this role, you will serve as the primary technical partner for our most strategic prospects and customers in the APAC region. You’ll play a dual role: driving complex technical engagements through end-to-end demos, migrations, and integrations, and accelerating ramp for new sales hires by codifying best practices. You will showcase our product’s value to prospects, uncover challenges and architect tailored solutions, drive successful sales evaluations, and champion customer needs internally.

Location & work mode

title: Account Executive, Mid Market (TOLA)
description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara , we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing - and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:
This is a dynamic, high energy role in which you will bring the Internet of Things to mid-sized customers, building Samsara 's business and bringing the benefits of sensor data to customers. Typical sales will be $20k to $100k, and involve POCs, multiple stakeholders, managing trials, multi-faceted pricing negotiations, and selling to executives and CXOs.
This role is open for candidates residing in the following US states: Texas, Oklahoma, Louisiana, Arkansas, Kansas, Missouri, Mississippi, Alabama. The role requires travel approximately 25% of the time.

You should apply if:

•
You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact-helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.

•
Your mantra is #alwaysbeprospecting: The world of operations is vast. Your customers are often out in the field and the best way to catch them is live on the phone. Samsara ’s top reps do constant research to find companies and contacts to expand their pipeline.

•
You have innate curiosity in how businesses work: One day you’ll meet with someone in waste management and the next you may be learning about the inner workings of a food distribution center. Our top sales team members seek to learn the ins and outs of the businesses they support in order to make a larger impact.

•
You are a life-long learner: Samsara sales are complex. You will need to learn about businesses where you previously had little knowledge. The payoff is big but you have to be willing to put in the work.

•
You build genuine relationships with your customers: The industries we serve have relied on pen-and-paper solutions for years and haven’t been met with the type of technology we offer. Our customers value earned trust and human relationships built over time.

•
You want to be with the best: Samsara ’s high-performance Sales culture means you’ll be surrounded by the best and challenged to go farther than you have before.

Minimum requirements for this role:

• 2+ years experience in a full-cycle, closing sales role

• Experience independently closing new deals larger than $10,000 in annual revenue

• All candidates must be located in one of the following US states: Texas, Oklahoma, Louisiana, Arkansas, Kansas, Missouri, Mississippi, Alabama.

An ideal candidate has:

Daraus entscheidest du im Team, bringst Vorhaben spürbar voran und lässt deine Kolleg*innen fachlich mitwachsen. Personalverantwortung hast du nicht, dafür umso mehr fachlichen Einfluss.
Deine Skills:

• Du gehst fachlich voran, ohne disziplinarisch zu führen. Du machst Komplexität für Kolleg*innen auf jedem Level greifbar und nimmst sie auf dem Weg mit, durch Feedback, Wissenstransfer und ständiges Sparring.

• Du beherrschst mindestens eine Ebene richtig tief, ob Kernel, Storage, Netzwerk oder Container-Runtime. Die übrigen verstehst du gut genug, um Wechselwirkungen zu erkennen. Du weißt, wie Kubernetes auf eigener Hardware läuft und was passiert, wenn es das nicht tut.

• Du analysierst Störungen bis zur Ursache, erkennst Muster hinter wiederkehrenden Problemen und definierst sinnvolle Monitoring- und Alerting-Regeln.

• Software-Engineering: Du baust Plattformkomponenten und Automatisierung selbst, idealerweise in Go, und kannst die Lösungen anderer fachlich bewerten.

Herausforderungen, mit denen wir uns gerade beschäftigen:

• Multi-Tenant-Hosting unter echter Last: Tausende Kunden-Workloads teilen sich unsere physischen Server - präzise Ressourcensteuerung (cgroups, Namespaces), CPU-/Memory-Scheduling sowie Storage- und Netzwerk-Performance auf Systemebene gehören zum Alltag.

• Automatisierter Node- und Cluster-Lifecycle: Vom Provisionieren der Hardware über Kernel- und Runtime-Updates (CRI-O, crun) bis zu unterbrechungsfreien Rollouts im laufenden Betrieb.

• Eigene Operatoren und Plattform-Services: Statt gemanagte Cloud-Dienste zusammenzustecken, entwickeln wir unsere Kubernetes-Controller, APIs und die Integration in Storage und Netzwerk (CNI, BGP) selbst.

Das bieten wir dir:

Tiefgang statt Standard

Wir arbeiten mit zukunftsweisenden Technologien und bauen Systeme, wenn nötig, lieber selbst, statt auf Fertiglösungen zu setzen. Das bringt Herausforderungen und ein technisches Niveau, das nicht alltäglich ist und dich fachlich weiterbringt.

Expertise, die ihresgleichen sucht

Du diskutierst auf fachlich höchstem Niveau, teilst dein Wissen und lernst gemeinsam mit anderen Experten. Unsere Expertise geben wir nicht nur intern , sondern auch gerne auf Konferenzen, Camps und in der Tech-Community weiter und gestalten so die Zukunft der Branche mit.

Wir lieben Tech

Bei uns triffst du auf Menschen, die Tech genauso feiern wie du. Diese Leidenschaft leben wir im Alltag - und darüber hinaus. Ob Open-Source-Engagement, Community-Arbeit oder der Support von Tech-Events: Wir sind aktiv dabei und bringen uns ein.

Technologische Verantwortung

Deine Expertise zählt. Du prägst Entscheidungen und bleibst nicht beim Offensichtlichen stehen. Du bekommst den Raum, deine Ideen umzusetzen, Systeme mitzugestalten und Verantwortung zu übernehmen - auf Augenhöhe und mit Rückhalt.

Technik trifft Menschlichkeit

Bei uns findest du die coolsten Kolleg*innen, jede Menge Humor und echten Team-Spirit. Zusammenarbeit ist für uns ein fester Teil des Daily Business. Auch nach Feierabend gibt es jede Menge Möglichkeiten, ob Fußball, Padel oder D&D - wer Lust hat, ist dabei.

Rundum-sorglos-Setup

description:
WHO ARE WE?

Launch Potato is the discovery and conversion company. We reach tens of millions of people every month through our brands, including FinanceBuzz, All About Cookies, and OnlyInYourState. We turn that attention into real outcomes for our partners, some of the world's leading companies.

Our mission: create predictable, high-value customer acquisition at scale by connecting discovery, intent, and performance across category-leading consumer brands in finance, travel, and entertainment.

We run profitable and bootstrapped, with a South Florida HQ and a remote-first team across 18 countries.

WHY JOIN US?

You own outcomes here, not tasks. We measure work by impact, not activity. The pace is real, and change is constant, so the people who do best turn change into opportunity instead of waiting for it to settle. Feedback runs direct and lands with respect. Ordinary people make themselves extraordinary at Launch Potato .

YOUR ROLE
You'll build the models that decide which carrier each auto insurance shopper sees on our click wall. The goal is to send every user to the carrier most likely to convert them, so carriers see our traffic convert and raise their bids. You'll also own the buying models behind our media spend, which are held to ROAS.
Carrier conversion data (quotes, policies and acquisition cost) is now coming back to us, and you'll be the one who puts it to work in production. The hard part is the data. Outcomes land weeks or months after the click, many sessions are sparse, the same shoppers come back, and the market drifts. Our bids also decide which users we win, so the model shapes the data it learns from next.
This is a hands-on individual contributor role. You frame problems directly with the business, find your own data, build and validate the model, and stay with it through deployment and monitoring. An ML engineer works alongside you on the production side. Auto insurance takes most of your time to start, and scope broadens to other verticals over time.
We're remote first, and most of the company works East Coast hours.
WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE
By day 60, you run our insurance marketplace media buying on your own.
By the end of your first year:

• Click wall serving that matches each user to the right carrier

• Carrier conversion data running in production models

• Automated marketplace bidding taken from proof of concept to scale

• A clear approach for repeat users and sparse sessions

• Production models that hold up through drift and changing objectives

• Output the business trusts and uses without rework

MUST HAVE

• 5+ years of hands-on applied data science with measurable business impact

• Your models drove paid media decisions: spend, bidding or ad serving. Attribution and reporting alone don't qualify.

• You built what's on your resume and can explain it down to the loss function and architecture choice, neural network fundamentals included

• You see how today's bids shape tomorrow's training data, and you've handled late labels, sparse features or drift

• You own models end to end: you find your own data, build through deployment and monitoring, and bring a point of view

• Expert Python and SQL

NICE TO HAVES

• Real ad budget spent in live auctions

• Large-scale ranking or recommendation systems

• Explaining tradeoffs to non-technical partners in plain terms

• Designing for auction feedback loops, selection bias and exploration

• Hands-on neural network work, such as embeddings of text, creative or user behavior

• AWS for data science: ECS, S3, Athena, SageMaker

• CI/CD deployment
